evidence:
Fetched https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.05217 and the HTML version (https://arxiv.org/html/2301.05217): Nanda, Chan, Lieberum, Smith, Steinhardt, "Progress measures for grokking via mechanistic interpretability", ICLR 2023. The title and authors match the bib entry.

What the paper reports:
- Sec 3 (setup): a one-layer ReLU transformer with d=128, 4 heads and 512 MLP units, P=113, trained with AdamW at lr 1e-3 and weight decay lambda=1.
- Sec 4.1: "the five key frequencies", k in {14,35,41,42,52}. Also: "The embedding matrix W_E is sparse in the Fourier basis -- it only has significant nonnegligible norm at 6 frequencies."
- Sec 4.2: W_L is approximately rank 10, which is 5 frequencies times sin and cos.
- App C.2.1: other seeds use other small sets, for example {2,9,19,31}.
- Sec 5.3: "our networks do not grok on the modular arithmetic task without weight decay or some other form of regularization".

So "a handful of frequencies with weight decay" is accurate.

Minor caveats:
- The weight decay is AdamW's decoupled decay, not an explicit l2 penalty on the loss.
- The model is a transformer, not the paper's one-hidden-layer model. The sentence says "trained networks", so it stays correct.

Notes are in /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/c4-nanda-handful/CHECK.md.

recommended_citations.why: Supports 'use a handful of frequencies'. Sec 4.1 reports five key frequencies {14,35,41,42,52} in a one-layer transformer at p=113 trained with AdamW, wd=1. Sec 5.3 says the networks do not grok without weight decay.

recommended_change: Nothing needs to change. Optionally make it concrete: "With ordinary weight decay they use a handful of frequencies (five, in a one-layer transformer at p=113 trained with AdamW) \citep{nanda2023progress}".
